evidence: Reachability: every capability is reachable. Runtime is node:22 with express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 preinstalled on NODE_PATH (environment/Dockerfile); /assets/seed_data.json is present in the agent image and instruction.md:15 tells the builder to copy it into /app because /assets is unavailable at runtime; network is public and CDN use is permitted (instruction.md:13, integration.md:12-14). Seed supports every seeded fact a criterion relies on: Lena (USR-CAN3) read_count 2 on APP-301 whose 3rd message is from USR-REC3 -> 1 unread, matching protocol Z; APP-101 has 120 messages, matching app_context.md:30 and hro_thread_latest/earlier; candidate wording and page size 30 are in the seed (hireops_rules.md:207-208). No graded capability is unreachable. Most rules are single-reading and precise (one-stage moves, reject/reopen, bulk board order hireops_rules.md:89-92, undo conflict list :96-100, 401/403/404 :21-23, version-based 409 :77-80, unread/seen definitions :151-166). Checked candidate ambiguities that turned out harmless: (a) whether re-ordering counts as a 'move' for undo-supersession - protocol B(11) is overdetermined because Mei already moved X in B(9), so any reading refuses that undo; (b) whether reopening is an undoable move - settled by ':97 restores a rejection reason that the move removed'; (c) whether hiring managers may add candidates - settled by :31 'A recruiter adds a candidate' and hro_mgr_early_refused; (d) 'get signed out' (instruction.md:7) - explicit sign-out and expiry are both covered by one design and polish hro_pol_session_resume accepts either prompt timing. Ambiguities that change grading: [1, P2] Where per-conversation unread counts appear. Brief: 'Unread counts need to be right for each person' (instruction.md:7); rules: 'Unread counts are shown per conversation and as one total for the person' (hireops_rules.md:154), with Board/Conversations/Activity as separate views (instruction.md:11). The natural reading puts per-conversation counts in the Conversations list and the total in navigation. Functional protocol U (tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:41) says 'Every reading in U is made without reloading, navigating or clicking in Rafael's page ... With Rafael's page on the Board, Tomas sends two messages; read Rafael's count on that conversation and his total', and hro_unread_counts (weight 2 of 58.5) 'Fails if any count is wrong ... or changes only after a reload or navigation'. Only an app that also shows a per-conversation count on the Board can provide that reading. The golden does that (solution/app/public/js/board.js:253, unread badge on each board card), but no public text asks for it. [2, P3] Message arriving while typing at the newest message. instruction.md:7 says 'If a message arrives while I am reading further up or halfway through writing a reply, leave my place, my draft and my cursor alone and just tell me there is something new', which on its face also covers a reader at the bottom who is typing: keep the scroll position and only notify. hireops_rules.md:158 says 'if they are at the newest message, it is shown and counts as read'. Polish hro_pol_live_thread (weight 3) fails if 'the view moves away from the newest message'. An app following instruction.md:7 literally keeps scrollTop fixed, appends the message below the fold and shows a notice. That app can be read as having left the newest message, and it leaves the message unread, which contradicts :158. Most implementers will follow the more specific rule, so the risk is low, but the two public texts read differently. [3, P3] 'keyboard focus stays on that card's controls' (hireops_rules.md:85) versus hro_refused_put_back's '(document.activeElement inside the card)'. If move controls live in an opened card-details panel (allowed: :104 'A card can be opened to show its details'), focus on the panel's move control meets the rule text, but a judge could fail it as not inside the board card element. No configured judge run exists to measure any of these; evidence is source reading plus golden source only.
counterexample: A conforming HireOps build: separate Board / Conversations / Activity views (as instruction.md:11 asks), the per-person total unread badge on the Conversations nav item updating live, and per-conversation unread badges in the Conversations list, also live, but no unread badge on board cards. In protocol U the judge holds Rafael's page on the Board and is forbidden to navigate. It sees the total rise by 2 but cannot read 'Rafael's count on that conversation' without navigating to Conversations. Once it navigates, the per-conversation count shows 2 correctly, but the criterion's own text ('changes only after a reload or navigation') invites a 0 on hro_unread_counts (2/58.5 functional weight) for an app that meets every public unread rule. A golden-shaped app passes only because of a board-card badge that no public text requests.
suggested_fix: In functional protocol U, either keep Rafael's page on the Conversations list with no conversation open (so both per-conversation and total counts are visible without navigation), or allow the per-conversation reading to be taken by navigating to the conversation list after the 15 s live check on the total. Separately, align instruction.md:7 with hireops_rules.md:156-160 (e.g. 'if I am reading further up, leave my place alone and tell me; if I am at the bottom, show it, but never touch my draft or cursor'), and loosen hro_refused_put_back to 'focus on a control of that card (on the board card or its open details)'.
